entries.title: I Kings 4:2
segments: A wise and good ruler, in the appointment of officers to take part in the administration of his government, will be especially careful to select such as are distinguished for wisdom and fidelity, and whose example and influence will be salutary to the people.

entries.title: I Kings 4:21
segments:
The river; Euphrates. 
 
Jehovah is a God of truth: when the word hath gone out of his mouth it standeth for ever; and though the fulfilment of his promises may be long delayed, in due time they will be accomplished.

entries.title: I Kings 4:22
segments:
Provision; for all his numerous household and the dependents of his palace. 
 
  Thirty measures; in the Hebrew, thirty cors.  The cor was ten ephahs.  Reckoning the ephah at one bushel and one twelfth, a cor would be a little less than eleven bushels.

entries.title: I Kings 4:24
segments:
This side the river; the west side. 
 
  Tiphsah; a city on the Euphrates. 
 
  Azzah; Gaza; on the south-west of Canaan towards Egypt.

entries.title: I Kings 4:25
segments: The true glory of rulers is not the extent of their conquests, nor the splendor of their establishments, but the happiness and prosperity of their people.

entries.title: I Kings 4:26
segments: Forty thousand stalls of horses; Solomon had "a thousand and four hundred chariots,"
, for which four thousand stalls would be a suitable proportion, according to the number given in
.  It has been the opinion of some expositors from ancient times that this latter number was the original reading.

entries.title: I Kings 4:28
segments:
Dromedaries; a species of camels, remarkable for speed; but others understand the original word of a breed of swift horses. 
 
  The place where the officers were; the words, "the officers," were applied by the translators.  We might better render, either the place where they--the horses and dromedaries--were; or, the place where Solomon was.

entries.title: I Kings 4:29
segments: Jehovah has infinite fulness, and he can so replenish the minds and hearts of his people with knowledge, wisdom, and grace, that they will shine as lights in the world, and pour forth the richest blessings on all generations, to the end of time.

entries.title: I Kings 4:33
segments: All the works of God manifest his infinite power, wisdom, and goodness, and may suitably engage a measure of the thoughts and investigations of the wisest among men.
